The Drawn-style fixtures are generated by executing the numerical path builder
and arrowhead functions from the local reference checkout. The JSON records its
commit. Regenerate from the repository root with:

```sh
bun crates/annotations/tools/generate-drawn-path-fixtures.ts /path/to/reference-checkout
```

The generator loads the reference source at runtime; the app does not bundle
that source or require Bun. Regular Rust tests use the checked-in coordinates.

The comparison covers two-pass rectangle and ellipse outlines, rounded fills,
zero-offset line and arrow bodies, and straight/curved arrowheads. It checks
coordinates within 0.00021 pixels (float and SVG rounding), then rasterizes both
paths through the export renderer and requires under 0.1% coverage difference.
This verifies shape geometry and export rendering; GPUI and browser antialiasing
can still differ.

Mouse ink has a separate `ink-paths.json` fixture generated directly from the
reference freehand pipeline and its mouse settings:

```sh
bun crates/annotations/tools/generate-ink-fixtures.ts /path/to/reference-checkout
```

Its 72 cases cover live and completed strokes at three widths: dots, duplicate
samples, short strokes, slow/fast movement, speed changes, curves, handwriting,
zigzags, loops, and tight reversals. Tests compare streamlined coordinates and
pressure-derived radii within 0.00001 pixels, then require less than 1% raster
coverage difference. The native renderer uses cubic semicircles in place of SVG
cap arcs; both app preview and export consume the same resulting filled path.
